mission: An industry-supported non-profit of leading AI developers focused on significant risks to public safety and national security, especially CBRN and advanced cyber threats. It identifies best practices and supports standards, advances safety science and research (including the AI Safety Fund), and runs information-sharing among firms, governments and others.

key_work.title: Frontier Capability Assessments (technical report)
key_work.plain_summary: Describes how member firms test models for capabilities that could raise CBRN, cyber or autonomy risks, as a snapshot of current industry practice.

key_work.title: Third-Party Assessments (technical report)
key_work.plain_summary: When and how outside evaluators should be brought in to assess frontier models.

key_work.title: Chain of Thought Monitorability (issue brief)
key_work.plain_summary: Industry view on preserving the ability to read and monitor models' reasoning as a safety tool.

key_work.title: Information Sharing, Incident Reporting, and Incident Response for Frontier AI Risks
key_work.plain_summary: Explains why these three tools are different and how they should fit together.

key_work.title: Thresholds for Frontier AI Safety Frameworks
key_work.plain_summary: How companies define the capability levels that trigger stronger safeguards.

key_work.title: Testimony: The AI Security Landscape (House Homeland Security subcommittee)
key_work.plain_summary: Chris Meserole's June 2026 written testimony on frontier AI, agents and cybersecurity.

status_note: founded July 2023 by Anthropic, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI; Amazon and Meta joined May 2024. Industry-funded 501(c)(6) that says it does not lobby.
status_raw: active — founded July 2023 by Anthropic, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI; Amazon and Meta joined May 2024. Industry-funded 501(c)(6) that says it does not lobby.
funding_note: Funded by member-company fees; also administers the AI Safety Fund (US$10m+ launched 2023).

people.role: Executive Director (since Oct 2023); previously Brookings AI & Emerging Technology Initiative

warnings.text: Frontier models could help develop chemical, biological, radiological or nuclear weapons.
Advanced AI can enable advanced cyber threats and some forms of dangerous autonomous behaviour.
AI agents and adversarial distillation create new security challenges.

recommendations.text: Developers should run frontier capability assessments and set clear risk thresholds in safety frameworks.
Use third-party assessments and share threat and vulnerability information across firms.
Develop standards for frontier AI risk management (e.g. supporting INCITS 594).
